summary: An uncursed genocide scroll reaches read.c:seffect_genocide, but js/read.js:seffects only records an unported gap. C then enters read.c:do_genocide, prompts for a species, marks its vital flags, and reports the result. Port the complete genocide effect family and source-ordered prompt/state path; the scroll case currently diverges at its first message boundary.

source.branch: read.c:seffect_genocide determines known scroll status, prints discovery feedback, then chooses do_class_genocide for blessed scrolls or do_genocide((!cursed) | (2 * Confusion)) otherwise. The selected uncursed, unconfused case passes REALLY=1 and answers newt. do_genocide accepts up to five names, handles refusal and forced player genocide, changes species flags, affects monsters and inventory, and can end the game. do_class_genocide handles the blessed path and has its own repeated class prompt.
callers: read.c:seffects SCR_GENOCIDE arm calls seffect_genocide after doread; js/read.js:seffects currently calls note_unported(read.c seffect_genocide).
sit.c throne arm also calls do_genocide(5) and js/sit.js records that path as unported; this is a separate active caller to wire when do_genocide is ported.
dependencies: mondata.c:name_to_mon is already ported in js/mondata.js and is needed for selected species names. insight.c:num_genocides and list_genocided are available in js/insight.js for conduct and question-mark responses.
mon.c:kill_genocided_monsters is currently a partial gap in js/do.js; C discards its result but its state effect must remain named as an unported gap until the full mon.c function is ported.
Check read.c:getlin prompt, monster-vitals flags, object inventory update, polymorph, death, and cursed monster creation in source order. Do not infer those paths from the selected newt case.

evidence: Current saved challenges/evaluations/20260927175933-v9.json leaves 7 of 31 screens unmatched, first at segment 0 step 24. A fresh scan at b6e28d15 reports note_unported(read.c seffect_genocide) and the same first screen mismatch; RNG totals alone do not prove the prompt and state path match.

The independently recorded C recipe challenges/cases/v9/genocide-scroll-selects-species.recipe.session.json wishes an uncursed genocide scroll, reads it, and answers newt. It is distinct from a hard-coded species fix; both blessed class genocide and cursed or confused branches remain part of the source family.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/read.c:seffect_genocide at lines 1722-1738 calls do_class_genocide or do_genocide; do_class_genocide at 2638 and do_genocide at 2826 implement the prompts and effects. read.c:seffects calls the wrapper at 2240; sit.c also invokes do_genocide(5) from a throne.
